fitAnalysis.assessment:
Weak Fit (30%): significant language and networking gaps make this role a poor match now.

**Strengths:**
- 11 years backend experience, including distributed fintech systems
- Kafka-based settlement service processing 40 million daily events
- PostgreSQL, on-call rotations, and incident reviews directly match JD

**Gaps:**
- Go and Rust are primary required languages; you have neither
- No networking experience: OSI layers, TLS, VPN, Linux networking
- Missing Kubernetes, ClickHouse, Grafana, and RFC authorship

**Recommendation:** Build Go proficiency and study networking fundamentals for 6-12 months, then target distributed-systems roles at companies like Cloudflare.

optimizedCVData.summary: Backend engineer with 11 years of experience designing and operating high-throughput, distributed, production-critical services in Java, Kotlin, and Python. At Lumen Payments, architected a settlement service processing 40 million events per day on Kafka and led a 4-engineer team through a 9-month microservices migration, owning on-call responsibilities and authoring post-incident reviews for 14 incidents. Brings a strong foundation in reliable system design, latency optimization, and event-driven architecture. Returning from a planned family caregiving break and actively current through an AWS Solutions Architect certification earned in 2024.

bullets: Designed and operated the settlement service in Kotlin and Spring Boot, processing approximately 40 million events per day on Kafka with high availability and fault tolerance.
Reduced p99 latency of the payment status API from 480 ms to 120 ms by migrating hot reads from PostgreSQL to Redis, improving customer-facing response times under peak load.
Led a team of 4 engineers through a 9-month migration from a monolith to 6 independent services, coordinating architecture decisions, code reviews, and phased production rollouts.
Owned on-call rotation for the payments platform and authored post-incident reviews for 14 production incidents, driving systematic reliability improvements across the service estate.
Built order and inventory services in Java and Spring, backed by PostgreSQL and RabbitMQ, supporting reliable asynchronous processing across distributed retail systems.
Introduced contract testing practices that reduced integration bugs caught in staging by approximately one third, improving deployment confidence and release cadence.
Collaborated with product and infrastructure teams on API design and service boundaries, contributing to a more maintainable and independently deployable service architecture.
Delivered internal web tooling for two client engagements in Java and JavaScript, working across the full delivery lifecycle from requirements through production deployment.
Collaborated directly with client stakeholders to gather requirements and iterate on solutions, building communication and cross-functional delivery skills early in career.
Maintained and extended existing Java codebases, applying code review feedback to improve code quality and adhere to team standards.
Took a planned career break for full-time family caregiving responsibilities.

Maintained technical currency by completing AWS Solutions Architect Associate preparation coursework, earning the certification in 2024, and participating in a Designing Data-Intensive Applications reading group.
Contributed bug fixes to an open-source Kotlin library, staying engaged with the engineering community during the break.

coverLetter:
Priya Raman
Toronto, Canada
priya.raman@example.com
+1 555 0176

October 12, 2026

Hiring Manager
Cloudflare

Dear Hiring Manager,

Keeping a distributed, production-critical system healthy at scale is a problem I know from the inside: at Lumen Payments I designed and operated a settlement service that handled roughly forty million events a day on Kafka, owned on-call for the payments platform, and wrote post-incident reviews for fourteen incidents. That operational depth is exactly what Cloudflare's Run What You Build model demands of the Egress team.

My eleven years of backend engineering span the full lifecycle the role describes: architecting services, leading design discussions, and shepherding complex migrations to completion. I led a team of four through a nine-month monolith-to-microservices migration, and I cut payment-status API latency significantly by moving hot reads from PostgreSQL to Redis, two experiences that map directly to building secure, highly-available distributed systems and debugging issues under production pressure. PostgreSQL is also a tool I use daily, which gives me a practical foothold into the data layer the Egress team relies on alongside ClickHouse and Grafana.

I would welcome the chance to talk through how my background in high-throughput event-driven systems translates to Cloudflare's egress infrastructure. I am available for an interview at your convenience.

Kind regards,
Priya Raman

Hi there,

My experience designing distributed, production-critical services in Kotlin and Java, leading a team of four through a nine-month monolith-to-microservices migration, and owning on-call responsibilities across a payments platform maps closely to the technical leadership and systems architecture work this role requires. My CV and cover letter are attached for your review. I am available for a call any weekday and would welcome the chance to discuss how my background fits the team's needs.

Best regards,
Priya Raman
